clubDescription: Swim Devon offers children’s swimming lessons with a child-centred approach, focusing on water confidence, technique and steady progress through the Swim England stages. Lessons in Lympstone use the pool at the Royal Marines Base with lane-based groups, so children can build skills in a more structured swimming environment rather than a splash-style session. It is an ideal activity for parents looking to improve their children's water confidence and their capability in the water, but note they are lessons and, while made fun and interactive for younger swimmers, they're structuredwith a view to progression, so the sessions require a termly commitment. The teachers are incredibly well-regarded and, for the younger groups, are in the water with children which supports their confidence as they're getting more familiar with the water and a larger, noiser setting. Arrive ready to swim (while there are changing rooms, they're limited at this venue) so most children arrive in a dryrobe or with loose clothing over their swimwear. Changing facilities are limited as Swim Devon do not have exclusive use of the changing rooms. Parents will need to pre-register and bring ID with them each week; you'll be met at the main gate 10mins before the lessons start and escorted, in a group, to the pool. The pool is maintained at around 28 but does vary - it's not the warmest pool but children are kept active during the sessions; it's worth knowing if your child is a definite warm-water swimmer, or might struggle with a busier group. If so, the Budleigh Lessons are taught in a smaller, warmer pool may be better suited to children who prefer that sort of introduction to swimming.

clubDescription: Run by Liz, Robin Wood Forest School is an outdoor nature-based session built around woodland play, exploring, making and learning through the seasons with the warmest welcome waiting for you. The appeal is obvious the moment you arrive; a natural, thoughtfully created woodland wonderland for children and teens that reveals new corners and activities as you explore it. Set on a sloping woodland, it's not well suited to buggies for smaller visitors, so bring a sling if they're not yet walking; but you can look forward to unstructured, free-roaming activities, that usually wrap up with a snack around the covered fitpit area. There is den building, mud kitchens, sticks, leaves, bug hunting, simple tools or crafts, creative and crafty activities, and the kind of open-ended play that changes with the weather and the site. It is likely to suit families who enjoy getting muddy, following their own ideas, noticing wildlife and being given more freedom than a standard indoor class or play session. Sessions run weekly during term-time with a host of lovely themed activities during half-term holidays. It's the sort of place you meet and make friends at; while many drop-in, the digital presence is limited, so it thrives through word of mouth recommendation; a gem to pass along to a friend.

clubDescription: Tenpin Laser Tag is a great activity choice when children are too old for soft play but still need to move and want something exciting to perk up a wet or dreary Tuesday. While this isn't an official club, it's 50% off every Tuesday, so if you've got laser tag in your wishlist, then Tuesdays are the most cost effective day for a battle! It’s a small indoor arena with LED lighting, sound effects, a smoke machine and infrared guns, so expect noise, a dark maze-feel, running about and a bit of competitive chaos. Brilliant fun for kids that love playing team based games, or in small group (min 2 people) and want to play 1:1. One to avoid for children who dislike dark, loud or high-energy spaces, and is worth check booking slots before heading over during peak party season, but there's lots to keep everyone occupied if it's a spontaneous trip and you need to wait for another booking to finish; bookings are usually 30mins long and a further discount is applied if you book for 2 x 30mins. There isn't an age limit as such, it's based on height; children need to be over 4ft (120cm) to play.

clubDescription: Tenpin Bowling is a safe bet at Marsh Barton when you need an indoor activity that mixed ages can all do together. While not officially a 'club', Tenpin offers 50% off on a Tuesday for bowling, which makes it a cheap and fun after-school activity, or something lightly competitive for the daytime if you're homeschooling. Younger children can usually join in with lighter balls and help from adults, while older ones get the competition element and can challenge themselves. There are 15+ lanes, but it's worth calling ahead if you have specific timings in mind as their Tuesday discount is often popular. clubDescription: Mud-ventures is an outdoor stay-and-play session for children aged six months to five years, run in Greendale's dedicated outdoor space alongside the farm shop on the Sidmouth Road. The idea is built around getting properly messy — mud kitchens, water play stations, sensory trays and a range of activity stations that change week to week, all using natural materials and open-ended resources that children can move between freely.
